claims.text: Enhanced local chemical short-range order is the primary mechanistic factor governing phase stability in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni high-entropy alloys.
Controlled thermal annealing can induce enhanced local chemical short-range order in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni alloys.
Enhanced short-range order stabilizes an optimal mixed FCC/BCC microstructure.
The mixed FCC/BCC microstructure is required for high-temperature strength.
The mixed FCC/BCC microstructure is required for environmental resistance.
The mixed FCC/BCC microstructure is required for radiation tolerance.
The mixed FCC/BCC microstructure is required for cryogenic toughness.
As-cast Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni alloys have a largely random atomic distribution and minimal inherent short-range order.
Rapid quenching after annealing can freeze in the high-temperature short-range-order state.
The relevant structural mediator is local chemical short-range order among elemental pairs having strongly negative mixing enthalpies.
Thermal energy during annealing drives local atomic rearrangements that enhance short-range order.
Enhanced short-range order alters the alloy's free-energy landscape.
Optimized short-range order stabilizes a fine mixed FCC/BCC phase structure.
Relative to the as-cast baseline, optimally induced short-range order will reduce phase separation and the occurrence of undesirable precipitates.
Relative to the as-cast baseline, optimally induced short-range order will maintain a mixed-phase microstructure.
Relative to the as-cast baseline, optimally induced short-range order will improve high-temperature strength and cryogenic toughness.
Relative to the as-cast baseline, optimally induced short-range order will improve radiation tolerance and environmental resistance.
Excessive annealing that produces macroscopic segregation will reverse the predicted microstructural and property benefits.
The hypothesis applies within an annealing-temperature window of 600°C to 1000°C, provided significant long-range segregation or precipitation is avoided.

Comparable property enhancement without increased short-range order, or confirmed increased short-range order without the predicted phase stabilization and property improvements, would falsify the hypothesis.
